advances: Exact additive growth for a specified original pair residual. This is not a dispersion credit bound for the entire three-plus-two menu.

proof:
In the genuine-contact application first shear by subtracting the affine interpolation of the two continuous marks, preserving every integer base and its volume. The positive deepest right mark is in the interior of its own fiber by 55a57b1cf55d0c87. For its critical pair the nonpositive margins at the left deepest mark follow from d368124f92bb0a43. Normalize the opposite continuous normals to $u,-u$ with $\lVert u\rVert=1$; the signs at the left mark give $b_\pm\ge0$. For the section argument itself only the displayed normal form and right-fiber interior are needed.

The missed set at base $z<1$ is the part of $C_z$ with $-(1-z)b_-<u\cdot x<(1-z)b_+$. Closing both inequalities changes only $d$-null cut boundaries. Since $1-z(t)=1/(1-t)$, scaling by $1-t$ gives $D_t$. The real base identity is
$$
z(s)=\frac{1-t}{1-s}z(t)+\frac{t-s}{1-s}.
$$
Take the corresponding Minkowski combination of the actual fibers and multiply by $1-s$. This gives $A_t+(t-s)C_1\subseteq A_s$. The body $E$ contains zero and has positive $p$-volume, since the anchor fiber contains a ball about zero. Adding $(t-s)E$ preserves the $u$-coordinate of every point in $D_t$, so the resulting point lies in $J$ as well as $A_s$. This proves $D_t+(t-s)E\subseteq D_s$, and it also proves the same inclusion of slices at each fixed coordinate. Taking the transverse vector zero gives nestedness.

We first prove the moment bound used in the integration. Let $h$ be nonnegative concave on a width-$w$ interval, positive inside, with $\int h^p>0$. Endpoint values may be replaced by the one-sided interior limits without changing the integrals. Thus take $h$ continuous on the closed interval. If $H=\max h$, the two line segments from a maximizer to zero at the endpoints lie below $h$; when the maximum is at an endpoint use the single segment of nonzero length. Their $p$-moment is $wH^p/(p+1)$, so $A=((p+1)\int h^p/w)^{1/p}\ge H$. Let $T(b)$ be the length fraction where $h>b$. It is concave on $[0,H)$: the superlevel sets are intervals, and the corresponding Minkowski interpolation of two such intervals lies in the intermediate superlevel set. Also $T(0)=1$. The value zero at $H$ preserves concavity up to that endpoint even if there is a maximum plateau; set $T=0$ above $H$.

Compare $T$ to $U(b)=(1-b/A)_+$. On $[0,H]$, $T-U$ is concave with value zero at zero, so $(T-U)/b$ is nonincreasing there for $b>0$. Beyond $H$ the difference is nonpositive. Thus it has at most one sign change from positive to negative. Layer cake and the definition of $A$ give $\int_0^\infty b^{p-1}(T-U)(b)\,db=0$. If the difference has both signs on sets of positive measure, use a crossing $c>0$ and multiply its zero-moment integrand by $b^{k-p}-c^{k-p}$ for $0<k<p$. The product is nonnegative, so $\int_0^\infty b^{k-1}(T-U)(b)\,db\ge0$. If there are not both signs, the zero moment forces equality almost everywhere. Integrating the tent tail therefore gives $\int h^k\ge wA^k/(k+1)$ for $0<k<p$, with $k=0,p$ immediate. An endpoint-zero tent of height $A$ has tail $U$ and attains all these bounds.

For positive-volume $D_t$, the $p$-volume root $h$ of its slices is concave by Brunn–Minkowski and positive at each interior height. Endpoints have no effect on the integrals, and the same moment proof applies. Brunn–Minkowski on the transverse inclusion and Fubini give $|D_s|\ge\int(h+ae)^p$. Expand the integer power and apply the moment bound term by term. The result is
$$
w\int_0^1 (Av+ae)^p\,dv
=w\,\frac{(A+ae)^{p+1}-(ae)^{p+1}}{(p+1)A}.
$$
For a nonempty zero-volume $D_t$, each nonempty slice contains a point, so its translated copy of $aE$ in $D_s$ has $p$-volume $a^p|E|_p$. Fubini gives the zero-volume bound. Zero width gives only nestedness and no positive lower bound from this argument. For $p=1$ the bound reduces to $|D_s|-|D_t|\ge a|E|_1 w$. At $z=-j$ use $t=j/(j+1)$ and $s=(j-1)/j$. The areas are $V_j/(j+1)^2,V_{j-1}/j^2$, the remote width is $w_j/(j+1)$, and $a=1/[j(j+1)]$. Multiplication by $j^2(j+1)^2$ gives the stated integer inequality.

For sharpness take an origin-symmetric full $p$-body $E_0\subset u^\perp$, $a_0>0$, and $K=\operatorname{conv}(E_0,\pm a_0u)$, $C=[-1,2]\times K$. Write $W=|K|$, so the total mixed volume is $4W$. At $(0,0)$ every nonvertical through-mark cap gets $W$ from the paired fibers $-1,1$ by central symmetry and $W/2$ from its own fiber. At $(1,0)$ use the pair $0,2$. Pure-base containing caps have mass at least $2W$ at either mark, and parallel tightening handles all containing caps. The pair at the right mark with $b_\pm=a_0/2$ has mass $3W/2$ in each cap: the trace at $-1$ is null and the paired contributions at $0,2$ sum to $W$. Its two margins sum to $a_0(z-1)$, so it covers all planes with $z\ge1$. At the left mark take independent $v_1,v_2$, $v_3=-v_1-v_2$, and caps with margins $v_i\cdot x-h_K(v_i)z/2$. Each has null trace at $2$, captures $W$ in the paired fibers $-1,1$, and gets $W/2$ on its own. Here $h_K$ is the support function and is positive on nonzero directions because $K$ has interior origin. Their summed margin is nonnegative for $z\le0$, hence this critical triple covers all left planes. Together the five caps bound global depth by $3W/2$, proving both genuine deepest contacts.

In the right pair's slab $J=\{|u\cdot x|\le a_0/2\}$ one has $E=E_0$. At $t=1/2,s=0$, $D_t=K/2$ and $D_s=K\cap J$. Their sections at $h=u\cdot x\in[-a_0/2,a_0/2]$ are respectively $(1/2-|h|/a_0)E_0$ and $(1-|h|/a_0)E_0$. Thus the transverse inclusion is equality, the remote slice-root profile is a tent, and every Brunn–Minkowski and moment comparison is equality. Each integer fiber has mass $W<2W$.
statement:
Let $C\subset\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^d$ be a compact convex body with $0\in\operatorname{int}C_1$, $d\ge2$. Given unit $u$ and $b_\pm\ge0$, use the pair $\pm u\cdot x+b_\pm(z-1)\ge0$. Put $J=\{-b_-\le u\cdot x\le b_+\}$, $E=C_1\cap u^\perp$, $z(t)=-t/(1-t)$, $A_t=(1-t)C_{z(t)}$ and $D_t=A_t\cap J$. The closed version of the missed pair residual at $z(t)$ equals $D_t/(1-t)$ up to null boundaries. For $0\le s<t<1$ with $C_{z(t)}\ne\varnothing$, one has $A_t+(t-s)C_1\subseteq A_s$, $D_t+(t-s)E\subseteq D_s$, and the same latter inclusion on each nonempty $u$-coordinate slice. In particular $D_t\subseteq D_s$.

Put $p=d-1$, $a=t-s$, and $e=|E|_p^{1/p}$, where $|\cdot|_p$ denotes the $p$-dimensional volume on $u^\perp$. If $D_t$ has positive $d$-volume $V$ and $u$-width $w$, put $A=(dV/w)^{1/p}$. Then
$$
|D_s|\ge w\,\frac{(A+ae)^{p+1}-(ae)^{p+1}}{(p+1)A}.
$$
If $D_t$ is nonempty with zero $d$-volume and positive width $w$, one has $|D_s|\ge a^p|E|_p w$. In dimension two the formula is $|D_s|-|D_t|\ge(t-s)|E|_1 w$, also valid for zero width or an empty remote residual. At integer sites $-j$, $j\ge1$, write $V_j$ and $w_j$ for the ordinary area and $u$-width of the unscaled closed residual, setting width zero for the empty set. Whenever the sections in question exist,
$$
(j+1)^2V_{j-1}-j^2V_j\ge j|E|_1w_j .
$$
The positive-volume bound is sharp in every $d\ge2$ even for actual adjacent globally deepest marks at $0$ and $1$, a genuine critical pair at $1$ and a genuine critical triple at $0$, with each integer fiber lighter than half the total.
title: Sharp transverse growth of an actual two-contact pair residual
